prize_parts.citation: for the invention and realisation of optical lattice atomic clocks reaching a fractional uncertainty of 10^-18
for the discovery of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos and the creation of neutrino astronomy with the IceCube observatory

statement.case_for: I have moved from my opening ordering, where the Higgs experiments came first, towards a configuration built on attribution I can actually defend. Optical lattice clocks (B029) are a discovery-plus-instrument achievement with an exceptionally clean metric: Katori's magic-wavelength idea made thousands of atoms usable as one quantum-limited oscillator, and Ye's group brought systematic uncertainty and stability to the 10^-18 level, with several independent laboratories now reproducing and comparing clocks. It is also physics that looks at nature: tests of constants, millimetre-scale gravitational redshift, dark-matter searches and the pending redefinition of the second. Pairing it with IceCube (B037) gives a second, entirely different kind of clue from nature, a new messenger. The diffuse high-energy neutrino flux is firmly established, the blazar TXS 0506+056 and Galactic-plane results show source astronomy has begun, and the cubic-kilometre detector in Antarctic ice was a bold concept that people doubted. These two achievements are distinct, each reaches the committee with strong confirmation, and together they use three names, which is the limit.
statement.case_against: The weakest part is B037. Halzen is the only credited name for what is a large collaboration with an AMANDA precursor and earlier deep-water and deep-ice pioneers, so a single-laureate part is exposed to the charge that it understates others, and the origin of most of the flux is still unknown, so I may be rewarding the window before the view. Pairing precision metrology with astroparticle physics could also look like an arbitrary pairing, chosen to fit the three-person limit rather than any scientific kinship. On B029, the neighbouring 2005 (comb) and 2012 (Wineland) prizes mean the committee may feel that atomic timekeeping has been honoured often. If B037 failed on attribution, I would fall back to B012 or B016, both of which are more mature but have their own credit problems.

responses.point: Optical lattice clocks are the measurement advance he values most: the magic-wavelength idea, the clarity of the metric, reproduction in several labs, and a Katori and Ye pair that is clean.
responses.response: I agree and it is why B029 anchors my configuration. Where I would qualify his argument is the field-opening claim: relativistic geodesy and dark-matter searches are still prospects more than results, so the citation should rest on the demonstrated 10^-18 performance and the cross-laboratory comparisons, not on future applications. I also note he ranks circuit QED second, and I do not think the 2025 prize makes B004 impossible, but I find the four-name attribution harder than the clock pair.

responses.point: IceCube opened neutrino astronomy with a real new observational window, but a single name under-represents a collaboration, the TXS association is only about 3 sigma, and the Galactic-plane result is recent, so maturity is arguable.
responses.response: I share his rank 2 and his worry, and I will not pretend the attribution is solved. The diffuse flux is by itself the discovery, confirmed by multiple analyses, so the TXS and Galactic-plane significance does not decide maturity. Where I differ is on his first choice: B013 is an elegant discovery, but van Paradijs and others are deceased or uncredited, and I would rather keep the Katori and Ye pair and Halzen than rely on a three-way split between satellite and ground follow-up. I also disagree mildly that the Higgs detectors deserve honour as instruments in their own right; the discovery was the physics, and leadership credit among thousands is the problem, not an answer to it.

responses.point: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene is a theory prediction followed by a decisive experiment and a new quantum behaviour in a material, with a large field and reproduction by many groups, though Cao and Fatemi are not credited.
responses.response: This is the strongest challenge to my configuration, and B031 is a serious candidate. Prediction followed by decisive experiment is how I like to see a discovery confirmed. My reservations are the unresolved mechanism of the superconductivity, a field that is still moving quickly, and a three-person attribution that leaves out the two lead experimental authors; those make me think it is a little early, not wrong. I would be persuaded to move it up if colleagues can show the allocation is robust. I also note that his B016 ranking, topological insulators, is mature and conceptually original, and that is why I keep it as an alternative.

responses.point: She ranks B029 first for precision and robust theory-experiment agreement, and also ranks topological insulators second while saying she defers to condensed-matter colleagues.
responses.response: I welcome her clock case because precision and agreement with theory are exactly what make a discovery trustworthy. On B016 I would press the question she leaves open: Kane and Mele are the decisive theory, but the HgTe prediction by Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang, the late Zhang's claim, and Hasan's three-dimensional work make a three-person set cut through a real dispute, so I would not prefer it over the clocks.

uncertainties: Whether Halzen alone is an acceptable credit for IceCube, or whether the committee should instead credit a different set of IceCube or AMANDA pioneers not on the shortlist.

Whether the committee prefers to give the whole prize to one field, and so pair B029 with a stronger-supported achievement such as B031 or B016, over combining precision metrology with neutrino astronomy.

Whether the outside expert assessments, which as Secretary I would normally commission, would confirm the independence of the Katori and Ye contributions at the 10^-18 level, and the status of source identification in IceCube.
How much weight the 2005 and 2012 prizes in neighbouring atomic physics should carry against B029.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from the provided profile. My PhD supervisor David Gross and co-author Thomas Van Riet work in string theory and cosmology, which is unconnected to every shortlisted candidate.
